status_summary: No HUD-specific order reassigning delegated authority or converting named HUD career leadership posts was found. Government-wide, Executive Order 14171 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-31) directed creation of a Schedule Policy/Career category, and OPM's final rule (published 2026-02-06, effective 2026-03-09) lets policy-influencing positions be placed in it while remaining career and merit-filled. Executive Order 14410 (signed 2026-06-03, published 2026-06-10) placed the positions listed in its appendix in Schedule Policy/Career; the appendix is published only as page images and whether HUD positions are included was not confirmed. HUD announced a chief of staff and two deputy chiefs of staff on 2025-06-27 without stating their appointment type.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14171 on policy-influencing positions was published in the Federal Register.
HUD announced a chief of staff and two deputy chiefs of staff.
OPM's final Schedule Policy/Career rule was published (91 FR 5580), effective 2026-03-09.
Executive Order 14410, signed 2026-06-03, was published, placing the positions listed in its appendix in Schedule Policy/Career.

title: Shift HUD delegated authority and leadership posts to political appointees
uncertainties: Executive Order 14410 (91 FR 34893, signed 2026-06-03) was re-read on federalregister.gov in review: Sec. 5(a) and (b) place the Appendix positions in Schedule Policy/Career and Sec. 5(c) requires agencies to notify covered employees within 7 days, but the Appendix (printed pages 34896 to 35124) is image-only on federalregister.gov and govinfo.gov and the text elsewhere never names HUD, so HUD coverage is unconfirmed. A news report on the order (just under 8,000 positions) does not name HUD. The CRS legal sidebar of 2026-03-26, read in review, confirms that Schedule Policy/Career positions remain career positions that lose chapter 75 and chapter 43 protections, and describes pending challenges: NTEU in D.D.C. (stayed pending the rule, with an amended complaint allowed within 14 days of a presidential placement order under a 2026-03-17 ruling) and PEER and four unions in D. Md.; the dockets were not opened and no later ruling was checked. HUD delegation orders are internal and were not found publicly. Schedule Policy/Career keeps positions career rather than converting them to political posts, so the match is partial. The OPM release carries no printed date. The record's absence component (no HUD-specific action) was not run through a full systematic check.
